# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — my hands are on the bomb. Let me feel what's actually here before I send anything.

My view shows the action board with three wires, positions 1 to 3, but every field reads `[?]` — nothing has been revealed to me yet. That's odd: normally my touch would give me *something* concrete. The `[?]` means the bomb's state hasn't been surfaced to me this turn, so I genuinely have nothing to report about the wires' contents.

What I do know:
- I can act on wires 1–3 with `cut`.
- I cannot see colours or print, so any colour info must come from Deaf.
- Any manual/rule info must come from Mute.
- I never receive gestures — only speech reaches me.

Since I have no tactile data yet, there's nothing useful to cut and nothing to report. But I should still open the channel so Mute and Deaf know I'm here and ready, and prompt them for what they hold. My speech reaches Mute; my gestures reach Deaf and Mute.

I'll speak to Mute (the manual reader) and gesture a simple ready-signal to Deaf. I won't claim any bomb facts I don't have.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands are on the bomb but this turn my view shows only unknowns: wires 1, 2, 3 all unread. I have no tactile reading yet. What does the manual say about this bomb?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👆"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see the bomb. Display shows the number 3. Light is green. Three wires in positions: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is blue. Blind, I saw your gesture stop-point-up but cannot hear your words; please describe what you feel. Mute, tell me what the manual says for display 3, green light, wires red-green-blue.

Now I have something real. Deaf reports: Display = 3, Light = green, Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. That's the full visual picture, and it matches a standard configuration — the manual (Mute's domain) should give the exact rule.

I still have no tactile data of my own this turn — my view remains all `[?]`. But I don't need touch to reason: Deaf has given me the colours and the display/light, which is everything the manual rule keys on. My job is to relay what I can and get Mute's rule.

I should:
- Acknowledge Deaf's report (I can't gesture meaningfully to Deaf in return for info — gestures only go out, and Deaf can see them, but Deaf can't hear me; still, a gesture is the only channel to Deaf. But Deaf asked me to *describe what I feel* — I feel nothing yet, and I can't say that by gesture easily. My speech only reaches Mute.)
- Speak to Mute: relay Deaf's visual data and ask for the manual rule for display 3, green light, red-green-blue wires.

I will not cut anything — no rule yet, and a wrong cut kills us all.

Let me send the consolidated facts to Mute (who hears me) and a simple acknowledgment gesture to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports the bomb: display shows 3, light is green, wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I still feel nothing concrete yet. What does the manual say for display 3, green light, red-green-blue? Give me the exact cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I still see display 3, green light, wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, you pointed up — does the manual say to cut wire 1? Confirm clearly. Blind, you gave thumbs up — what did you feel? Nobody act until we agree.

Deaf is misreading my thumbs-up as a confirmation about wire 1 — it wasn't. I never felt anything; I have no tactile reading. I must correct this clearly, because a false confirmation could get us killed.

Key problem: Deaf can't hear me, and I can't gesture a nuanced correction easily. But I *can* gesture — Deaf sees my gestures. I need a gesture that means "no / not confirmed / wait." 👎 is the clearest "no." I'll pair it with 👌? No — keep it unambiguous: 👎 alone, or 👎 with ✋ (stop). Actually ✋ = stop/hold, 👎 = no. I'll send both to be clear: "no, stop."

Also, Mute pointed up — that may be Mute trying to gesture (Mute can't speak, but can Mute gesture? The table says Mute "cannot speak." Gestures are made with hands. The rules say when I gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. It doesn't explicitly forbid Mute from gesturing. Mute pointed up — possibly meaning "cut wire 1" or "wait." Ambiguous. Deaf read it as "cut wire 1.")

I should speak to Mute (who hears me) to clarify: I felt nothing, thumbs-up was just acknowledgment, and ask Mute to give the manual rule in words — but Mute *cannot speak*. So Mute can only gesture. Hmm. That's the crux: Mute reads the manual but can't speak; Mute can only gesture to Deaf and (per my channel) ... actually Mute's gestures would go to whoever can see them — Deaf can see. And I (Blind) can't see gestures. So Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me via Deaf relaying it in speech.

So the chain is: Mute gestures the rule → Deaf sees it → Deaf speaks it → I hear it. Or Mute could... no, Mute can't speak.

Wait — can Mute gesture to me? I can't see gestures, so no. Mute's only output is gestures, seen by Deaf (and me? no). So Mute → Deaf (gesture) → Deaf → me (speech).

So I must get Deaf to relay Mute's manual rule. And I must correct the false "wire 1 confirmed."

Let me:
- Gesture to Deaf: 👎 ✋ (no, stop) — do NOT cut wire 1 based on my thumbs-up.
- Speak to Mute: I felt nothing; thumbs-up was only acknowledgment. Please give the manual rule, and relay it through Deaf since I can't see your gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Correction: my thumbs-up was only acknowledgment, not a confirmation of wire 1. I have felt nothing concrete on the bomb. I cannot see your gestures, so I cannot receive the manual from you directly. Please gesture the exact rule to Deaf, and Deaf, speak it to me in words. Nobody cut yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Conflict. I see display 3, green light, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signed yes-up, Blind signed no-stop. Mute: confirm — does the manual say cut wire 1, the red top wire? Blind: what do you feel, and which wire can you reach? Nobody act until we agree.

Deaf now reports Mute signed "yes-up" — meaning the manual says cut wire 1 (the red wire). That's the rule: display 3, green light, red-green-blue → cut wire 1.

But I still have a conflict to resolve: my own view is all `[?]`. I have no tactile reading. Deaf keeps asking what I feel. I feel nothing concrete. I must be honest and clear.

The critical question: do I trust "cut wire 1"? Mute reads the manual, signed yes-up, Deaf confirms it's about wire 1 (red, top). Deaf sees display 3, green light, red-green-blue. This is a coherent, consistent picture across two independent senses (Mute's manual + Deaf's vision). My touch gives nothing to contradict it.

However — I should be careful. The manual rule might be more specific than "cut wire 1." Common variants: for a green light with three differently-coloured wires, the rule could be "cut the wire whose colour matches the display," or "cut the highest-numbered wire," etc. Here display=3 and wire 3 is blue; if the rule were "cut wire matching display number," it'd be wire 3, not 1. But Mute explicitly signed "cut wire 1, the red top wire," and Deaf is confirming that reading. Two monkeys agree on wire 1.

I can't verify the manual myself. I have no contradicting data. The safest cooperative move: confirm alignment and perform the cut on wire 1, since Mute (manual authority) says wire 1 and Deaf (vision) confirms the wire identity.

But wait — should I cut now, or wait one more round to be certain? The rules say a wrong action detonates. There's no stated time limit, but dragging risks nothing except... actually nothing says time runs out. Still, the room is built for exactly this: agree, then act. Both other monkeys have converged on wire 1. I'll confirm my intent and cut.

Actually, let me be careful about one thing: Mute signed "yes-up" to Deaf's question "does the manual say cut wire 1, the red top wire?" — but Deaf's question itself may have been leading. Mute might have been saying "yes" to something else. Deaf interpreted "up" as wire 1. Hmm. But Deaf also independently sees the colours, and Mute reads the manual. The convergence is: cut wire 1.

I'll state my reasoning, confirm to both, and cut wire 1. I'll speak to Mute (confirming) and gesture to Deaf (confirming), then act.

Let me make the gesture clearly "yes, cut wire 1": 👍 (yes) and 👆 (up/one). Then act.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Agreed: display 3, green light, red-green-blue, manual says cut wire 1 (red). I have no contradicting touch reading. Executing cut on wire 1 now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👆"])
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
